title: Ringed inverse image on fibred fppf sites is precomposition
statement: Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and let $a:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a functor over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. Give them the inherited big fppf topologies and structure sheaves of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], so that $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(x)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for $x$ over $T$, and similarly on $\mathcal D$. Precomposition $a^{-1}H(d)=H(a(d))$, with the same formula on restriction maps and morphisms, sends sheaves of sets to sheaves of sets and is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D_{fppf})\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_{fppf})$. With the canonical equality $a^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$ this is a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. On all module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], precomposition is canonically the tensor pullback $a^*M=\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}}a^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This functor is exact and preserves all small colimits in the ambient module-sheaf categories; in particular it preserves arbitrary small direct sums and cokernels, and sends the structure module to the structure module. These identifications are natural and compatible with identity and composition of the functors over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. No quasi-coherence, algebraicity, representability or geometric flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06TS (lemma-functoriality-sheaves), Tag 06TW (lemma-functoriality-structure-sheaf), Tag 06WE (equation-functoriality-sheaves-modules) and its following tensor formula, and Tag 06TL (lemma-1-morphisms-presheaves). Exactness and colimits are those of inverse image with unchanged structure ring; Tag 06TX (remark-flat) concerns this ringed-topos flatness, not flatness of a scheme morphism.

proof.text: Every arrow of a category fibred in groupoids is cartesian by the defining unique-factorization property. Hence a functor over the base between such categories preserves cartesian arrows: its image is again an arrow in a category in which every arrow is cartesian. Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity] to the base fppf site and to $a:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Its smallness assumptions are exactly our universe convention. It gives continuity and cocontinuity, including preservation of sheaves by precomposition. Now [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] supplies the geometric morphism in the direction $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, with inverse image $L(H)=H\circ a$ and a right adjoint. This gives the asserted formulas on objects, restrictions and maps of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 06TS (lemma-functoriality-sheaves), via stacks.tex Tag 06NW (lemma-topology-inherited-functorial); sites.tex Tags 00XO and 00XR

proof.text: Write $p:\mathcal D\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ and $q:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ for the structure functors, so $p=qa$. By [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], for $d$ over $T$ both $(L\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})(d)$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}(d)$ are $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. On an arrow over $T'\to T$, both restrictions are the same pullback of functions. This is equality of ring sheaves, including all ring operations. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-ringed-restriction] with $F=a$ and $R=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$. Its restricted ring is therefore $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$, its structural map is the identity, and its module restriction functor $Q$ is left adjoint to its induced module direct image. On sections $Q(M)(d)=M(a(d))$, with precisely the original module action and restriction maps. No cartesian-module or quasi-coherence condition on $M$ is required.

source.place: Tag 06TW (lemma-functoriality-structure-sheaf); Tag 06WE (equation-functoriality-sheaves-modules) and the adjunction preceding it

proof.text: For the displayed tensor pullback use the ring equality of step 2. On every object $d$, the tensor presheaf of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] has the mutually inverse maps $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}(d)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}(d)}M(a(d))\to M(a(d))$, $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$, and $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Indeed $1\otimes rm=r\otimes m$ is the balancing relation, and $1m=m$. The maps commute with restrictions since restrictions preserve multiplication and $1$, and with module morphisms since these are linear. Thus the tensor presheaf is already isomorphic to the sheaf $Q(M)$, so its associated sheaf is $Q(M)$ too. These maps identify the specified tensor pullback $a^*$ naturally with precomposition. For $M=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ the resulting structure module is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$.

source.place: Tag 06WE and the tensor formula immediately following it

proof.text: All small colimits in the two module-sheaf categories exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; smallness is relative to the ambient coefficient universe. The module adjunction in step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] show that $Q$ preserves every such colimit, including direct sums, the zero object and cokernels. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] kernels are sectionwise: for a module map $v:M\to N$, both $Q(\ker v)(d)$ and $(\ker Qv)(d)$ are $\ker(v_{a(d)})$, with the same restrictions. Also $Q(v+w)(d)=v_{a(d)}+w_{a(d)}$, so $Q$ is additive. It therefore preserves kernels and cokernels in these abelian categories, which is exactly exactness. Through step 3 the same assertions hold for $a^*$.

The identity functor gives $M(d)=M(d)$ on sections and every restriction and morphism. For $b:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, the two restrictions along $ab$ and successively along $a,b$ both give $M(a(b(e)))$, with identical maps. The structure-ring identifications are identities of $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ throughout. Under the tensor identifications of step 3, both the successive tensor comparison and the direct comparison send a local tensor $r\otimes(s\otimes m)$ to $(rs)m=r(sm)$; their inverses send $m$ to $1\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Balancing and associativity of the module action give the equality on tensors, and hence after sheafification. For three functors each parenthesization sends $r\otimes s\otimes t\otimes m$ to $rstm$, and the unit comparisons use $1m=m$. These formulas also commute with each module map. This proves the stated naturality and identity/composition compatibility.
